title: Hybrid attention kernel profiler and regression mitigation
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Build a hybrid attention-kernel profiling and selection layer that: 1) continuously profiles incoming prefill/decode workloads across sequence lengths and precisions, 2) chooses the lowest-latency / cost kernel variant (vendor kernels, custom Triton kernels, and our reference GEMM-based kernel) at request time, and 3) detects and mitigates regressions by falling back to safe kernels and triggering alerts. This ticket focuses on the profiler, decision policy, runtime fallback mechanisms, and an automated canary rollout for the selector. Motivation: recent regressions observed when new optimized kernels were selected for short-sequence workloads (P95 decode regressions and memory fragmentation leading to OOMs). We need an operational selector that is robust to kernel warm-up effects, KV-cache alignment, and quantized execution paths.
acceptance_criteria: Profiler collects per-kernel latency, GPU SM utilization, and peak memory for common shapes (seq=8,32,128,512,2048) and precisions (fp16,int8) into telemetry every minute
Selector policy chooses kernel variant per-model + sequence-length bucket with <5% misprediction vs empirical best on holdout benchmark
Automatic fallback triggers when p95 latency for selected kernel exceeds baseline by >20% for 5-minute window or when memory error/alloc failure observed
Canary rollout plan implemented: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on SLO breaches
Docs and runbook updated; at least one on-call drill executed and logged
comments: 2026-03-01 Sofia Martinez: Created ticket after postmortem for 2026-02-26 regressions where a v3 optimized kernel increased p95 for short-decoding workloads. See postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/2026-02-26-attn-regression
2026-03-03 Liam O'Connor: Initial profiling harness (attn-prof) landed in experimental branch. microbench PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4523

2026-03-05 Performance notes from synth runs: v3 kernel shows best throughput for seq>=512 and batch>=4; for seq<=32 v3 is 10-25% slower than baseline_gemm due to kernel launch overhead and divergence. Observed increased GPU memory fragmentation with v3 at high concurrency.

2026-03-07 Design review feedback (PM + Reliability): prefer runtime decision to be deterministic per-request shape rather than purely statistical. Added policy to require minimum sampling window (5 minutes) before switching for a model/shape combo.

2026-03-09 Implementation update: added fallback hook for memory allocation failure and KV cache mismatch detection. Hook triggers immediate kernel swap to baseline and creates alert in Opsgenie. PR with fallback code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4589
2026-03-11 Canary plan drafted: rolling percentages + automated checks (p95 latency, error rate, GPU memory errors). Dashboard proto: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/attn-kernel-selector

2026-03-12 QA: ran canary on staging for Llama-2-13B quant-fp16 profile. Observed kernel warm-up effect where the first 30s shows higher p95; added warm-up sampling (2x warm-up batch) to mitigate noisy decisions. Logged warm-up behaviour: https://docs.redwood.ai/attn-kernel-warmup
decision_log: 2026-03-04: Decision to implement hybrid selector in C++ runtime layer to avoid extra RPC for hot-path; selector exposes simple policy DSL to experiments team.
2026-03-06: Chosen buckets for decision keys: (model_id, precision, seq_bucket, batch_bucket, decode_v_prefill_flag). Buckets: seq: [<=32, 33-128, 129-512, >512].
2026-03-08: Rejected always-prefetch warming: pre-warming costs too much for low-traffic models. Adopted adaptive warm-up for canaries and cold-model first N requests only.
2026-03-10: Rollback threshold set to p95 increase >20% AND error rate +1% absolute over baseline during a 10 minute window; both conditions required to reduce false positives from noisy benchmarks.
